policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the qere, which is what MACULA Hebrew projects; the alternative is the ketiv written in the Leningrad Codex.

decisions.evidence: ASV 'Jashub' renders the qere יָשׁוּב (shureq, -ub); the ketiv ישיב would yield 'Jashib'. The 'other' note concerns Puvah/Iob in Gen 46:13, not this name.
ASV 'Jeush' renders the qere יְעוּשׁ; the ketiv יעיש would yield 'Jeish'. No note is mapped.
ASV 'Birzaith' renders the qere בִרְזָיִת (-aith); the ketiv ברזות would yield 'Birzoth'. No note is mapped.

Qere וְרָהְגָּה and ketiv ורוהגה differ only by a plene waw inside the name; both transliterate as 'and Rohgah', which is what ASV prints. The 'other' note (Shomer, v. 32) concerns a different name. Base qere projection retained.

ASV 'Jehubbah' renders the ketiv יחבה with initial yod and no conjunction ('Rohgah, Jehubbah, and Aram' — no 'and' before the name); the qere וְחֻבָּה would yield 'and Hubbah'. The 'other' note (Shomer, v. 32) concerns a different name.
